keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's Georgia row starts in 724 with 7,076 km2 on the north-western Georgian coast. The Abasgia page says that by the 4th century the Abasgians occupied the land between the Gumista and Bzyb rivers; it gives no 8th-century extent. The years 724-777 belong to the predecessor Principality of Abasgia, before this dossier's life (778-1008); the shape is left as drawn.

23,893 km2: Abasgia with Egrisi after Leon II's union of the 770s ('Leon II exploited this dynastic union to acquire Lazica in the 770s'; 'Towards circa 778, Leon II won his full independence'). The page gives no area; stands.

24,443 km2. The page lists the eight duchies Leon II made (Abkhazia proper, Tskhumi, Bedia, Guria, Racha, Takveri, Svaneti, Argveti, Kutatisi) and a coast 'about 300 Greek miles long' in the 10th century; no area, so stands (unverified).
29,158 km2, +19 percent at 875 with no page for the step; George I (864-871) 'began eastward expansion' and nothing is dated. Stands (unverified).
30,138 km2, +3 percent at 886; no page. Stands (unverified).

The eastern strip is therefore not direct territory.

region.text: Abasgia, the Principality of Abasgia's core

ledger.note: 778: Leon II wins independence from Byzantium and founds the Kingdom of Abkhazia at Anacopia. 'Towards circa 778, Leon II won his full independence with the help of the Khazars'; the infobox dates the kingdom to the 780s and the first king's reign 780-828.

region.text: Egrisi (Lazica), acquired through the dynastic union

ledger.note: c. 778: Leon II adds Lazica (Egrisi) to Abasgia. 'Leon II exploited this dynastic union to acquire Lazica in the 770s.' The Lazica dossier ends its last shape in 777; this dossier starts the kingdom in 778.
786: the court moves from Anacopia to Kutaisi (infobox 'Anacopia (778-786), Kutaisi (786-1008)').

region.text: a significant portion of Kartli, 'bringing his borders close to the Arab-controlled Tiflis'

ledger.note: 904: Constantine III annexes a significant part of Kartli. 'In 904 he had finally annexed a significant portion of Kartli, bringing his borders close to the Arab-controlled Tiflis' (the Kingdom of Abkhazia page says 'In about 908'). In 905 he allied with Kvirike I of Kakheti and the two divided Hereti's major strongholds (a division of strongholds, not drawn). Who held the annexed land is not on the page; the Iberian kings were his rivals for Inner Iberia. [Reviewer eu-19-x, 2026-10-31: counterpart set to kingdom-of-the-iberians: the Kingdom of the Iberians page says that in 904 'Adarnase was dispossessed by Constantine III'.]

914: Abkhazia dominates Tao-Klarjeti. After Smbat I of Armenia was hanged at Dvin in 914, 'This was the beginning of almost sixty years of Abkhazian dominance over Tao-Klarjeti'; Adarnase was reduced to his Tao lands and became Constantine's vassal.

930s: George II breaks Kakheti's Kvirike II. George backed the Gardabanian nobles against Kvirike II and 'succeeded in dispossessing Kvirike of his principality in the 930s'; the Kingdom of Abkhazia page adds that Kakheti and Hereti 'briefly accepted Abkhazian suzerainty'. The year 935 is a midpoint of the page's decade.

c. 960: Kakheti wins back its lands. The Principality of Kakheti page: under Kvirike II the Abkhazian king raided Kakheti, in 959 Kvirike's brother Shurta handed him Ujarma, and 'Kakheti later reclaimed its lands after a truce with Leon III' (undated); the George II page has George dying in 957 on an expedition against Kvirike's rebellion. The year 960, the start of Leon III's kingship on that page, bridges the silence.

c. 973: the Abkhazian dominance over Tao-Klarjeti ends. The page gives 'almost sixty years' from 914; no end year is dated (David III installs Bagrat III in Kartli in 975, Kingdom of the Iberians page).

978: the Bagrationi succeed the Anchabadze. 'Bagrat III, of the Bagrationi line, took the throne in 978' as Theodosius III's successor; the Kingdom of the Iberians page says David III installed him as prince of Kartli in 975 and later as king of Abkhazia (978).

region.text: Abkhazia, Egrisi and Kartli, merged into the Kingdom of Georgia

ledger.note: 1008: Bagrat III unites Abkhazia and Iberia. 'In 1008, Bagrat succeeded on the death of his natural father Gurgen as the King of the Iberians', uniting the two kingdoms into the Kingdom of Georgia; official style 'the Kingdom of the Abkhazians and the Iberians' (Kingdom of the Iberians page).

wars.name: Arab expedition of Marwan II into Abkhazia
wars.outcome: Marwan's expedition entered Abkhazia in 735-736 but 'dysentery, floods, and resistance under Leon I, with Iberian and Lazic allies' forced the Arabs to retreat.
wars.note: Before the kingdom's founding in 778; listed because the page dates it and the Georgia row begins in 724.

wars.name: Constantine III's Kartli and Hereti campaigns

zones.text: a significant portion of Kartli up to the Arab-controlled Tiflis

wars.outcome: Constantine III annexed a large part of Kartli in 904 and, allied with Kvirike I of Kakheti, invaded Hereti in 905 and divided its major strongholds; Adarnase IV and Bagrat later defeated and captured Constantine.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Abkhazia page dates the Kartli annexation 'about 908'.

wars.name: Abkhazian hegemony over Tao-Klarjeti
wars.outcome: After Emir Yusuf's invasion of Armenia in 912 and Smbat I's death at Dvin in 914, Adarnase of Tao was left a vassal of Constantine III: 'almost sixty years of Abkhazian dominance over Tao-Klarjeti'.

wars.name: George II against Kvirike of Kakheti
wars.outcome: George II dispossessed Kvirike II in the 930s with the Gardabanian nobles; he died in 957 on an expedition against Kvirike's rebellion in Kartli and Leon III made an inconclusive peace; Kakheti recovered its lands after a later truce.
wars.note: Dates are the George II page's (930s, 957); the Principality of Kakheti page adds 959 and an undated truce with Leon III.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary of any kind; Kartli and the Kakheti side are readings of the pages' prose.

notes: Cliopatria row: the 'Georgia' Name carries this kingdom for 724-1009 (shapes georgia_724..980); eu-19-b splits that row and should leave these shapes to this dossier (or point at it). Shapes 888-979 (up to 86,640 km2, east to 47.8 E) draw Kartli, Kakheti and Hereti as direct land; the pages support only the 904 Kartli annexation (Constantine III page; the Abkhazia page says about 908) plus vassal/ally relations with Kakheti (935-957) and Tao-Klarjeti (914-c.973), so the shapes are adjusted to new keyframe kingdom-of-abkhazia_904. Unexplained Cliopatria steps (875, 886, 947, 960) have no page. The Kingdom of the Iberians page says George II 'appointed his son Constantine as viceroy of Iberia' in 917, which the George II page dates 923 (Constantine 923-926, then Leon 926-957); the later page is followed. Wikipedia infobox for Abasgia is 64-786 and the Abkhazia page gives the kingdom's first king from 767 (infobox) or 780 (table): 778 is the page's 'circa 778'. Needs dossiers: principality-of-abasgia (predecessor, to 777), kingdom-of-kakheti-hereti (Kvirike's line, to 1010). No Abkhazia dossier area could be compared (no page gives km2). Gazetteer: 'Kartli' resolves as a region; no new names needed.
